decision.question: does the demo-stage system need a default width cap, and if so where
decision.verdict: No cap belongs in ext/demo's stage.css (it correctly leaves width to the page grid); the real uncapped risk is ext/catalog's browse.css, ".browse-band > .page-previews", whose auto-fit 1fr max already admits in its own comment that a short band stretches cards to about a thousand pixels each at 3440 - exactly the owner's complaint. Proposed default: cap the per-card max at roughly min(28em, 1fr) instead of a bare 1fr, so a short band leaves gutter the same way wall()'s auto-fill already does. The alternative (cap the band's own outer width instead of the card) should stay opt-in, not default - it only wins when a band is guaranteed a near-full row of cards.
decision.evidence: measured headless at 3440 on 10 of 23 flagged stages via a private PORT=8126 server; the web/ page's 2-card wall confirmed compact (257px cards each, auto-fill working as designed); browse.css lines 45-57 document the tradeoff directly in its own comments
decision.confidence: medium - grounded in the codebase's own comments plus 10 live measurements, but the proposed fix itself has not been tried or measured post-change

**The site study is built: 68 things scored, a demo-stage verdict, and a bug found in the scout process itself.**

`ext-b.json` had wrongly re-studied six modules already covered by `ext-a.json` (JSONL, Omnibox, Panel, Research, Saver, Timeline) and skipped the real six (catalog, demo, depth, drawer, editor, files) - those were never scouted by anyone. Fixed it myself: researched the missing six the same way a scout would (full readme, full page.js, doc/ file names) and rebuilt ext-b.json. Also found and fixed 9 of its 15 blurbs hard-truncated at a fixed ~85-character cut - would have shipped broken fragments into `blurbs.json`.

[study.md](/framework/ai/2026-09-18/site-study/study.md) - the full sorted table, ten least clear, 23 flagged stages, 11 things with no demo, and the five-sentence demo-stage verdict with real measurements.
[blurbs.json](/framework/ai/2026-09-18/site-study/blurbs.json) - 68 url-to-blurb entries for the rail builders.
[scouts/](/framework/ai/2026-09-18/site-study/scouts/) - the eight validated, reconciled source files.

The demo-stage finding: `ext/demo`'s own stage CSS has no width cap at all - the cap decision belongs to the page around it. Measured 10 of 23 flagged pages headless at 3440. Most turned out fine (multi-card walls reflow into more columns instead of stretching). The one real, currently-uncapped risk is exactly what `ext/catalog/browse.css`'s own code comment already names: a short band (2-3 cards) stretches those cards to fill the row - the comment even says "a band of three on a 2750px wall draws three cards a thousand pixels wide," almost the owner's own words. Proposed fix logged as a `decision` line: cap the per-card max instead of the bare `1fr`, the same way `wall()`'s `auto-fill` already avoids the problem elsewhere (confirmed live: /web/'s two-card wall stayed a compact 257px per card).

Left deliberately open: the fix itself (a one-line CSS change in `ext/catalog/browse.css`) was not made - my fence is `site-study/**` only, and proposing it as a decision line is what the brief asked for, not shipping it. 13 of the 23 flagged stages were not individually measured (the ten chosen span a representative mix of Doc pages, imagine/ programs, and layouts/ pages).
